newsitem.title: USA: Unabomber suspect's lawyers want evidence thrown out.
newsitem.headline: Unabomber suspect's lawyers want evidence thrown out.

text.p: Lawyers defending Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski asked a federal judge on Monday to throw out all of the evidence that investigators seized from his Montana cabin, local news reports said.

A motion filed by defence lawyers in U.S. District Court in Sacramento late on Monday alleges that the FBI's search of Kaczynski's cabin last year was illegal and that false evidence was used to obtain the search warrant, San Francisco's KCBS radio station reported. The motion seeks to throw out all of the evidence taken from the cabin, it said.
Court officials and defence lawyers could not immediately be reached for comment. It is common for defence attorneys to file motions to suppress evidence.

Kaczynski, a 54-year-old former mathematics professor, was arrested in April 1996 at his rustic one-room cabin in Montana. He is accused of being the shadowy Unabomber, who killed three people and injured 23 during an anti-technology bombing campaign between 1978 and 1995.

Prosecutors and investigators have said they found extensive evidence at his cabin incriminating Kaczynski, including bomb components and a diary that they say contained his "detailed admission" to each of the 16 Unabomber attacks.
Kaczynski has been charged in Sacramento with four bombings, two of them deadly. Kaczynski, who is being held in Sacramento, has pleaded not guilty. His trial is scheduled to start in November.

Prosecutors have six weeks to respond to the defence motion to throw out evidence seized in the search. A hearing on the motion is scheduled to be held before U.S. District Judge Garland Burrell in Sacramento on May 16.
